success_patterns: Compare near-duplicate options by their exact logical strength: a bound on a liminf exponent is not automatically a fixed-constant bound at that same exponent.
Separate subsequential compactness of structural parameters from convergence of metrics or preservation of geometric properties; stronger conclusions need separate support.
Distinguish almost-sure convergence to one of several listed limits from a positive-probability claim for each particular limit.

patch.reasoning: The existing skill already emphasizes exact hypotheses and option wording. These additions clarify three consequential distinctions exposed by the trajectories: liminf bounds versus endpoint rates, parameter compactness versus metric compactness, and possible limits versus positive probability for each limit.

edits.target: - Preserve the exact form of asymptotic assertions: note cutoffs, the order of iterated limits, and whether the claim uses a limit or limsup. Do not silently replace a truncated approximation with convergence to a full series.
edits.content: - Keep exponent bounds distinct from endpoint power bounds: a statement such as \(\liminf_{N\to\infty}\log A_N/\log N\ge\alpha\) gives \(A_N\ge N^{\alpha-\delta}\) eventually for every \(\delta>0\), but does not by itself give \(A_N\ge cN^\alpha\) for a fixed \(c>0\). The latter does imply the exponent bound.

edits.target: - Before using a special case or counterexample to reject a claim, verify that it satisfies every structural assumption in the question, such as nondegeneracy, regularity, parameter restrictions, and the stated measure. A case that violates a hypothesis does not refute the claim.
edits.content: - Separate compactness of the stated parameter space from compactness of additional data: a convergent subsequence of structural parameters alone does not establish convergence of metrics or preservation of a geometric property in the limit.

edits.target: - Translate each option into its logical form before comparing it. Track quantifier order and dependencies: “for every target, there exists a witness” differs from one witness working for every target, and a constant that may depend on a parameter differs from a uniform constant. Distinguish all parameter values from sufficiently large values, and a whole class from a restricted subclass.
edits.content: - For a finite list of candidate limits, almost-sure convergence to one member of the list does not imply that each member occurs with positive probability. Treat an all-indices positive-probability claim, and any eventual-membership condition attached to it, as additional assertions to verify.
